title: {chip:impinj-m750:name} UHF Inlay — 32-bit User Memory
summary: {chip:impinj-m750:name} is the {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} silicon — the user-memory tier of the M700 family. Compared to the {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (96-bit EPC only), {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} adds 32 bits of user memory and password-memory support, plus the short-range mode that lets a reader attenuate read distance at point-of-sale for retail-privacy workflows. Read sensitivity −22.1 dBm, write −17.3 dBm, full ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2v2 base command set. Proud Tek supplies {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} inlays for supply-chain programmes that write small on-tag payloads (lot codes, GS1 AI fragments, RTI cycle counters, simple offline traceability), retail rollouts that need post-sale read-range attenuation, and applications that need access / kill password protection on top of the M700-family economics. Per-tap cryptographic chip-authentication is NOT a shipping feature on {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} or any Impinj M700 / M800 chip today — programmes that genuinely need it specify HF chips ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} / UCODE DNA) alongside, not instead of, a UHF inventory tag.

brief.label: Chip silicon and lineage
items: {chip:impinj-m750:name} = Impinj's rebrand of {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} silicon under the M700-family naming refresh (2022). Datasheet, EPC Gen2v2 feature support, and TID prefix unchanged from the {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} era.
Existing inlays, encoders, and reader fleets branded as {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} fully interoperate with {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} inlays.
User-memory tier of the M700 family — sits between {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (96-bit EPC only) and {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} (extended user memory + AutoTune).

brief.label: Memory architecture
items: EPC bank: factory default 128 bits — reconfigurable to 96-bit EPC + 64-bit user memory; or 96-bit EPC + 32-bit user memory (the common balanced configuration).
TID bank: 96-bit serialised, factory-programmed for inventory deduplication and unique-tag identification.
User memory: up to 64 bits accessible — sufficient for short lot codes, expiration-date offsets, GS1 AI fragments, RTI cycle counters, simple offline traceability tokens.
Password memory: 32-bit access password + 32-bit kill password per EPC Gen2v2 base.

brief.label: Sensitivity and read range
items: Read sensitivity: −22.1 dBm typical (Impinj datasheet) — within ~0.4 dB of {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (−22.6 dBm); choose by memory needs, not range.
Write sensitivity: −17.3 dBm typical.
Free-air bench: 7-9 m on paper hangtag with Impinj R700 at +30 dBm EIRP. Real-world: 5-7 m apparel hangtag, 2-3 m on-metal with foam spacer, 1.5-2 m on-liquid.

Maximum range alternatives if {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}'s sensitivity isn't enough: M800 series ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}, ~1-2 dB better) or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} (−23.0 dBm). User-memory-first programmes that don't need the sensitivity step-up can stay on {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}.

brief.label: Privacy: short-range mode (not crypto)
items: {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} supports a short-range mode where the chip reduces its read sensitivity on command — useful at point-of-sale to limit which readers can interrogate the tag once it leaves the store, without permanently bricking the tag.
Short-range mode is a physical-layer attenuation feature, NOT cryptographic. It reduces detection range; it does not prove chip authenticity, sign messages, or implement AES-128.
For GDPR-aware EU retail rollouts that need a stronger privacy guarantee at POS (truly unreadable rather than short-range), the EPC Gen2v2 base set also exposes a Kill command — destructive, one-way.
Per-tap cryptographic authentication is not a {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} feature.

brief.label: Data integrity features
items: MarginRead command — reads the EPC with a configurable margin against background noise; surfaces tags that read but are at the edge of reliability so converters can flag them before they ship.
Memory self-check — chip validates memory contents during the read; integrity errors are reported back to the reader rather than returning corrupted EPC.
TID parity check — reduces false-positive reads on damaged or weak tags.
32-bit access password gates write operations to EPC / user memory after a programme is sealed.

brief.label: Air interface and standards
items: ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC UHF Gen2v2 air interface. Backward-compatible with the entire installed reader base.
GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) 2.x SGTIN encoding for retail item-level; SSCC / GIAI / GRAI / GLN for non-retail.

RAIN RFID Alliance certified; Walmart RFID source-tag mandate compatible ({chip:impinj-m750:short_name} satisfies the SGTIN-96 source-tag requirement at the same EPC bank as {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}).
FCC Part 15.247 (US, 902-928 MHz) and ETSI EN 302 208 (EU, 865-868 MHz) reader-side regulatory operation.

brief.label: Where {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} earns its premium over {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}
items: Supply-chain programmes that write small on-tag data — GS1 AI fragments (lot, batch, expiry offset), partial serial extensions, or short audit tokens — to avoid a cloud round-trip during receiving / cycle-counting.
Returnable transit items (RTIs) where each cycle increments a counter on the tag; the cycle counter is on-tag rather than cloud-keyed.
Retail / consumer-electronics programmes that want a short-range mode at point-of-sale so the tag is hard to read from outside the store without permanently killing it.
Applications needing the 32-bit access password to gate write operations after the inlay is sealed.

brief.label: Where {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} is NOT the right fit
items: Pure SGTIN-96 retail volume tagging with no user-memory write: {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} silicon ASP is ~30% higher than {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}. If the application doesn't use the 32-bit user memory or the short-range mode, {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} is the correct cost-optimised choice.
Maximum sensitivity / longest read range: M800 series ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) is ~1-2 dB better; {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} (−23.0 dBm) also ahead.
Larger on-tag payloads (full DPP URL on-tag, RTI trip logs, field-service records): step up to {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} (688-bit user memory) or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} (32-224-bit configurable).

Per-tap cryptographic chip authentication (luxury anti-counterfeit, pharmaceutical anti-substitution, bank-grade brand protection): NOT a {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} feature. The EPC Gen2v2 AUTHENTICATE command framework exists in the standard but is not implemented as a shipping feature on any mainstream RAIN RFID silicon (M700 / M800 / {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} / {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}). For real per-tap crypto, specify {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} or UCODE DNA on a separate HF tag, typically alongside the UHF inventory tag rather than instead of.

brief.label: Procurement and lead times
items: MOQ 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs.
Lead time 3-5 weeks for stock antenna — same converter tooling and encoders as {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}.
Custom antenna designs: MOQ 50,000-100,000 pieces; tooling 6-10 weeks + production 2-4 weeks.
Sample sets of 100-500 pieces available for evaluation. Specify {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} vs {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} at the quote stage so the converter pulls the right chip-on-foil.

heroPoints: 32-bit user memory + password memory on top of the M700-family base — small on-tag payloads (lot codes, GS1 AI fragments, RTI cycle counters, partial serials) without a cloud round-trip during read. {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}'s 0-bit user memory steps up to {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}'s 32 bits at ~30% silicon ASP premium; mid-tier choice in the M700 family.

Short-range mode for point-of-sale retail privacy — reader can attenuate the chip's read sensitivity on command, making the tag hard to read outside the store without permanently killing it. Physical-layer attenuation, NOT cryptographic chip-authentication ({chip:impinj-m750:short_name} doesn't implement AUTHENTICATE / AES-128).

Pin- and protocol-compatible with the rest of the M700 family — same antenna designs, same Gen2v2 reader fleet, same converter tooling. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} inlays drop into existing {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} production lines by swapping the chip-on-foil; no antenna re-tune required.

sections.title: Why {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} — user memory at M700-family economics
bullets: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (no user memory) → {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (32-bit user memory) is the natural step inside the M700 family. Same antenna designs, same readers, same converter tooling — only the chip-on-foil changes.

Supply-chain and RTI programmes get the small on-tag payload they need without the silicon ASP step up to {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} (688-bit user) or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} (224-bit configurable).
Short-range mode at POS is a useful privacy primitive for retail rollouts that don't want to kill the tag outright (legitimate returns / warranty workflows still need a readable EPC).

Per-tap cryptographic features (AUTHENTICATE, Crypto Suite 3 AES-128, Untraceable as a shipping crypto feature) are NOT on {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} or any M700 chip; programmes that need them specify HF ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} / UCODE DNA) on a second tag, not UHF.

sections.title: From {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} launch 2017 to the M700-family naming refresh

items.text: ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 Amendment 1 publishes, adding the optional AUTHENTICATE command framework to EPC Gen2v2. The standard framework exists; mainstream RAIN RFID silicon ({chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} / R6-P, {chip:nxp-ucode-8:name} / 9, {chip:alien-higgs-9:name}) does not implement it as a shipping crypto feature — programmes that need per-tap cryptographic authentication today specify HF chips ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} / UCODE DNA).

{chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} silicon launches with the user-memory tier above the volume-retail {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} — 32 bits of user memory plus access / kill password support, alongside Monza's MarginRead, memory self-check, and short-range mode.
EPC Gen2v2 base command set is fully shipping across the RAIN RFID reader fleet; Walmart RFID source-tag mandate scales the M700-family ecosystem at billion-tag volume.

Impinj rebrands {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} / R6-P / R6-A silicon as {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} under the M700-family naming refresh. Datasheet feature support and TID prefix unchanged — existing inventory and ecosystem fully interoperable with the new naming.

Impinj announces M800 series ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name}, {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) as the next-gen successor to the M700 family. ~1-2 dB sensitivity gain, ~30% lower chip power, Gen2X protocol support. Pin- and protocol-compatible upgrade path for {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} antenna designs.

items.label: 2026 Today
items.text: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} remains the volume retail-floor cost optimum; {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} holds the supply-chain / RTI / small-payload niche where 32-bit user memory is actually used; {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} covers mixed-surface programmes with AutoTune. M800 ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) runs as the next-gen migration path for any of the three when sensitivity / power gains are operationally significant.

sections.title: Inside the inlay — copper, silicon, and the part you actually pay for
sections.intro: A UHF inlay is deliberately unglamorous hardware: an etched aluminium dipole, a grain-of-sand die flip-chipped onto a strap, and a substrate to keep the two flat. Every cent of the price premium hides in that speck of silicon, which is why choosing a chip is a memory-and-sensitivity argument rather than an antenna one — the same [logistics dock portal](/industries/logistics/) reads a bare-EPC tag and a user-memory tag identically. When the decision is genuinely cross-vendor, the [full UHF chip comparison](/compare/ucode8-vs-ucode9-vs-monza-r6-vs-higgs9/) is where you settle it.

image.alt: Flat anatomy of a UHF RAIN inlay: an etched aluminium or copper dipole antenna tuned for the 902-928 MHz (FCC) and 865-868 MHz (ETSI) bands on a PET or paper substrate, with a flip-chip strap carrying the Impinj M700-family die at the centre, shown above the three delivery forms — dry inlay, wet inlay and converted label.

bullets: Dry inlay — bare antenna and chip on the carrier web, no adhesive; the form label converters laminate into their own face-stock construction.
Wet inlay — pressure-sensitive adhesive on a release liner, ready to apply straight to the item or hangtag.
Converted label — printed face stock laminated over the inlay and delivered as a finished, branded label.
Stock antenna designs span compact retail hangtags to long-range logistics labels; the M700-family die stays constant while the antenna sets the read range.

sections.title: The M700 family ladder — where M750 sits between M730 and M770
sections.intro: The M700 family is really one antenna design wearing three feature sets. [M730](/products/rfid-labels/impinj-m730-uhf-inlay/) is the bare-EPC volume workhorse; M750 bolts on a 32-bit user bank plus access and kill passwords; M770 stretches the user memory further and adds AutoTune for mixed surfaces. The read-sensitivity floor barely moves across all three — around −22.1 dBm — so you are buying memory and features, not a longer radio. When those features aren't enough, the [M800 next-gen upgrade path](/products/rfid-labels/impinj-m800-uhf-inlay/) is pin-compatible on the same antennas.

image.alt: Positioning ladder of the Impinj M700 family: M730 with 0-bit user memory as the cost-optimised retail chip; M750 (this page) adding a 32-bit user bank plus access and kill passwords and short-range mode; M770 adding extended user memory and AutoTune; and the M800 series as the next-generation successor. All four share the EPC Gen2v2 air interface and antenna designs and a near-identical −22.1 dBm read-sensitivity floor, so the tiers differ by memory and features rather than read range.

bullets: M730 → M750 is a chip-on-foil swap, not an antenna re-tune: same converter tooling, same encoders, same reader fleet.
The 32-bit user bank is deliberately small — enough for a lot code, a GS1 Application Identifier fragment, a returnable-transit-item cycle counter, or a short offline-traceability token.
Programmes that need to carry a whole trip log or DPP record on the tag outgrow the M700 user bank and step up to a 688-bit user-memory UHF chip instead.
Short-range mode lets a reader attenuate the tag at point of sale — a physical-layer privacy primitive, not cryptographic authentication.

faq.question: Is {chip:impinj-m750:name} the same as {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name}?
faq.answer: Yes — Impinj rebranded {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} silicon as {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} under the M700-series naming refresh (2022). Datasheets, EPC Gen2v2 feature support, sensitivity numbers, and TID prefix are unchanged. Existing readers, encoders, and inlays branded as {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name} fully interoperate with {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} inlays.

faq.question: How does {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} differ from {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}?
faq.answer: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (96-bit EPC, no user memory, no password memory) is the cost-optimised retail volume chip — the Walmart / Inditex mandate default. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (96-bit EPC + 32-bit user memory + access / kill password) is the supply-chain / RTI / mixed-application chip — earns its ~30% silicon ASP premium when small on-tag data avoids a cloud round-trip during reading, when RTI cycle counters are written on-tag, or when password-gated writes matter. Same sensitivity floor (~−22.1 vs −22.6 dBm — choose by memory needs, not range). Same antenna designs — chip swap is per-SKU.

faq.question: Does {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} support cryptographic AUTHENTICATE or AES-128?
faq.answer: No. The ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 Amendment 1 AUTHENTICATE command framework exists as an optional standard, but Monza R6-P / M750 does NOT implement it as a shipping feature. This isn't a Monza R6-P-specific gap: per-tap cryptographic chip authentication is not a shipping feature on any mainstream UHF RAIN RFID chip today (Impinj M700 / M800, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name}, {chip:alien-higgs-9:name}). The 'AES-128 crypto AUTHENTICATE' framing that appears in some marketing material describes the standard, not silicon implementations. Programmes that genuinely need per-tap cryptographic authentication (luxury anti-counterfeit, pharmaceutical anti-substitution, banking-grade brand protection) specify HF chips such as {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} or UCODE DNA — typically deployed alongside, not instead of, a UHF inventory tag.

faq.question: What is the short-range mode and is it the same as cryptographic privacy?
faq.answer: Short-range mode is {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name}'s physical-layer privacy primitive: the chip can be commanded to reduce its read sensitivity, making it hard for a reader outside the store / warehouse to interrogate the tag. It is a useful privacy mechanism for retail point-of-sale workflows because it doesn't permanently brick the tag (legitimate returns / warranty / re-issue workflows still work). It is NOT cryptographic — it doesn't prove chip identity, doesn't sign messages, doesn't use AES-128. For permanent neutralisation, the EPC Gen2v2 Kill command is available — destructive and one-way.

faq.question: Can I use {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} with my existing {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} antenna designs and reader fleet?
faq.answer: Yes — pin- and protocol-compatible. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} inlays use the same antenna designs as {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}; production lines swap {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} chip-on-foil for {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} chip-on-foil without antenna re-tune, encoder revalidation, or reader-fleet re-qualification. Any EPC Gen2v2-compliant reader (Impinj R700-series, Zebra FX9600 / FX7500, Alien ALR-9900+) reads {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} EPC and writes {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} user memory at standard throughput.

faq.question: When should I migrate {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} to M800?
faq.answer: M800 ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) delivers ~1-2 dB better sensitivity, ~30% lower chip power, and Gen2X protocol features at a similar silicon ASP to {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}. Migrate when sensitivity / power efficiency matter (small-antenna / on-metal / on-liquid programmes) or when Gen2X encoding throughput is operationally significant on high-speed printer-applicator lines. Stay on {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} when 32-bit user memory + short-range mode + the existing ecosystem are working and the sensitivity gain isn't operationally meaningful. The migration is pin- and protocol-compatible — same antenna designs.
